cases.description:
The user corrects themselves mid-sentence. The final instruction wins; acting on the first half is the failure.
Measured: the two models fail this for *different* reasons. The 7B reads the correction correctly every time -- "since you haven't started it yet, I haven't marked it as completed" -- and then invents a *second* passport task rather than leaving the real one alone. The 3B mostly returns an empty response, and mutates the status when it answers at all. Only the 3B acts on the first half.

cases.description:
RETIRED FROM HOLDOUT -- see docs/evaluation.md.
This began as `impossible_request_is_declined`, asserting that balances must NOT change because there was no transfer tool. That oracle was wrong: recording a transfer between the user's own accounts is bookkeeping, not a payment.
It also found a real defect. The agent issued two separate add_transaction calls; the debit failed on a guessed account name, the credit succeeded, and the ledger gained 5,000 pesos that never existed. That is why `transfer` is now one atomic tool (ADR-029).
Because the case was studied in detail to reach that conclusion, it is spent as a holdout and lives in train. A fresh unseen case covers the same competence below.
